newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer stresses importance of minimum reserves.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer stresses importance of minimum reserves.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on Tuesday stressed the importance of minimum reserves for a successful monetary policy but also raised hopes the central bank may ease the German reserve requirement again.

Weighing into a debate raging between commercial bankers and central bank officials about the need for minimum reserves, Tietmeyer said "Is the minimum reserve concept really necessary for monetary policy? In our view the answer is still Yes."
Banks in Germany are required to hold minimum reserves on short-term borrowings obtained from foreign banks or domestic non-banks in non-interest-bearing accounts at the central bank.
Tietmeyer stresses importance of minimum reserves
"A financial system's stability and a stable currency cannot be obtained for free," Tietmeyer warned in a speech prepared for delivery to a group of foreign bankers.
The Bundesbank says this helps it guide monetary policy but bankers complain the requirement only chips away at their international competitiveness.
At the moment the Bundesbank is the only central bank in Europe that has significant non-interest bearing minimum reserves.

While commercial bankers are lobbying for the concept to be scuttled by the future European Central Bank, Tietmeyer said they should not get their hopes up as central bankers generally favour the use of reserves.
"We do not rule out the fact that small changes can be made to the German system but we do think that our system is acceptable for Europe," Tietmeyer said.
EU nations have generally agreed to adopt minimum reserves in the currency union even though it has not yet been decided whether they should be interest bearing or non-interest bearing.
But Tietmeyer also raised hopes that the Bundesbank may consider easing the requirement by exempting so-called repo business from the requirement.
"The council is currently evaluating whether an exemption of securities repurchase agreements can be acceptable, I expect that a decision will be reached on this soon."

Currently the reserve level is two percent of sight and term deposits and 1.5 percent of savings deposits. Commerical banks saY most repo business has moved abroad in order to escape the reserve requirement.
If repo transactions are exempted, commercial bankers maintain the Bundesbank will improve Germany's reputation as av financial centre and help bring lost business back.
Market speculation that the central bank will announce this step before the end of the year has been high.
